# Rebuilding over a sitemap without lastmod dates hangs, and pairs dates across entries

## Context

Found while running neomjs/pages#10's dry runs for neomjs/neo#19047. A second pages build at an unchanged engine version spun at ~100% CPU inside step 7's `buildScripts/docs/rebuildContentIndexesAndSeo.mjs`, and I killed it after 24 minutes. A pages build writes a sitemap without `<lastmod>` values ("Git history is shallow or unavailable"), and the next build reads that file back as `existingSitemapPath`.

Measured on `dev@18b473b6e8`:
- `getSitemapXml({existingSitemapPath})` over the previous 1.5 MB, 19,293-URL sitemap was stopped by SIGTERM at 45 s.
- The same call without `existingSitemapPath` returns in 1 s.

## The Problem

`getExistingSitemapLastmodMap` (`buildScripts/docs/seo/generate.mjs:456–471`) runs one global pattern over the whole file:

```js
/<url>[\s\S]*?<loc>(.*?)<\/loc>[\s\S]*?<lastmod>(.*?)<\/lastmod>[\s\S]*?<\/url>/g
```

`[\s\S]*?` is not bounded by `</url>`, which causes two faults:
1. **It hangs.** When an entry has no `<lastmod>`, the pattern searches to the end of the document from that entry, and from every later one. A file with no dates at all is scanned quadratically.
2. **It pairs the wrong entries.** An entry without `<lastmod>` takes the next entry's `<lastmod>`, and that next entry is consumed. For `<url><loc>A</loc></url><url><loc>B</loc><lastmod>D</lastmod></url>` the map is `{A → D}`, not `{B → D}`.

Both have shipped since `dde5acf77f` (#12261, 2026-05-31), so 13.0.0 and 13.1.0 carry them. In practice, pages' `update-neo-version-force` hits the hang whenever it re-runs at an unchanged engine version, because the previous lastmod-less sitemap is still in the tree.

## The Architectural Reality

- `getSitemapXml` (`generate.mjs:866`) calls the function only when git history is unusable and an existing sitemap path is given (`:907–910`).
- The function is module-private and has no spec. `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docs/seo/Generate.spec.mjs` covers the release-note helpers only.

## The Fix

Match one `<url>…</url>` block at a time, then read `loc` and `lastmod` inside that block. Map an entry only when both exist. That is linear in the file size, and it never pairs across entries. Export the function so a unit spec can reach it without running git.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: For an entry without `<lastmod>` followed by an entry with one, the map holds only the second entry's `loc` and date. Red on `dev`.
- [ ] AC-2: A sitemap of thousands of entries without `<lastmod>` returns an empty map. The speed claim comes from the structure (each block is read once), plus an outside-CI measurement on a real lastmod-less sitemap. No CI timing ceiling.
- [ ] AC-3: A sitemap where every entry is dated still maps each `loc` to its `lastmod`. *(Corrected 2026-09-24: reading a block with `<lastmod>` before `<loc>` is new behaviour. The old pattern required `<loc>` first, and the generator always writes it first.)*

## Out of Scope

- Where lastmod comes from for a corpus copy with no git history. neomjs/pages#10 records that question.
- The `lastmod` policy itself (#12259).
